newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Roldan points finger at ex-state secretary.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Roldan points finger at ex-state secretary.

text.p: Ex-Spanish Civil Guard chief Luis Roldan testified on Tuesday that former secretary of state for security Rafael Vera had organised illegal financing for the Socialist party when it was in power.

Roldan, the first civilian head of the paramilitary Civil Guard in its 150-year history, is on trial for embezzlement and corruption charges related to illegal Civil Guard contracts and activities. Roldan told the Supreme Court that Vera had asked him to open a number of Swiss bank accounts into which he paid commissions received by companies in exchange for awarding contracts. These funds were used to finance the Socialist party.
Before Swiss judge Paul Perraudin who is investigating illegal operations in a number of Swiss bank accounts, Roldan described himself as a mere collector of commissions.
Roldan's lawyers said Roldan testified that the accumulated 1.8 billion pesetas ($13.69 million) was returned to the government in 1994.
Roldan fled Spain in 1994 to avoid trial but was eventually recaptured nearly a year later in Laos.
Vera has also been indicted on charges relating to corruption.

Jose Maria Aznar and his centre-right Popular Party took office in May after early elections forced on his Socialist predecessor Felipe Gonzalez by mounting corruption scandals and revelations of a "dirty war" against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) rebels. ($1=131.5 Peseta)
